claims.statement: EU implementing rules under Regulation 2024/573 extend certification requirements for stationary air-conditioning and heat-pump equipment to covered alternative refrigerants as well as F-gases.

Polish enterprises performing third-party installation, service, repair, or decommissioning of stationary refrigeration, air-conditioning, and heat-pump equipment containing F-gases need an enterprise certificate for the covered activities.
Poland operates a Central Register of Operators with equipment cards for covered equipment, creating a persistent asset-record workflow rather than a one-off certificate task.

contrary_evidence: CRO and UDT already provide the authoritative registers and certification services, so the product cannot charge merely for access.
The UDT enterprise-certificate page still references an older implementing regulation in parts, signalling a changing national implementation layer that increases maintenance burden.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the family installer as a design partner, recruit 10 paid firms through one wholesaler or training partner, then scale via distributor bundles and technician-to-operator invites
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 1800 firms at 4200 PLN ARR plus 40 operator accounts at 30000 PLN ARR gives 8.76m PLN ARR; at 22% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 75% founder ownership, equity could exceed 5m PLN in years 6-8. Validate European portability and do not double-count retained cash.
economics.founder_time: 2.5-4 hours per day initially; productise onboarding before serving more than 20 firms and outsource regulatory review
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 82-90% software gross margin after onboarding templates; occasional audit support priced separately
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 8-12 months if 60 firms average 350 PLN monthly and channel commissions stay below 25%; validate churn and support load
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 199-499 PLN per company per month plus 12-30 PLN per active regulated asset; operator portfolio tier from 1200 PLN per month
economics.retention_or_repeat: Assets require service over years, certificate scope changes, records persist for audits and warranties, and technicians repeatedly work across the same installed base

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal service and refrigerant history tied to technician credentials and asset identity makes audits, warranty work, resale, and future service easier, increasing lock-in and enabling anomaly benchmarks
fingerprint.customer: Polish micro and small HVAC, heat-pump, and refrigeration installation and service companies plus multi-site equipment operators
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Bundle or refer through refrigerant wholesalers, heat-pump distributors, certification trainers, and the family renewable installer network; technicians pull operator customers into the asset portal
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Certificate-aware field-service app, refrigerant ledger, customer evidence pack, CRO preparation, and audit binder sold as recurring vertical SaaS
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The service company pays per technician and active asset when it records regulated work; larger operators pay for portfolio oversight
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A certified technician completes installation, repair, leak checking, recovery, or decommissioning and must leave a consistent evidence trail and update the relevant equipment record

founder_fit: Direct design-partner access through the parents' renewable-energy installation company
Combines regulated data, automation, and a measurable field workflow
Can start within 5 hours per day and below 100000 PLN
Channel and product-led expansion reduce reliance on high-energy founder sales
risks: Technicians may resist data entry unless the app also saves time on customer documentation and invoicing.
Incorrect credential logic or equipment thresholds could cause compliance harm.
Field-service incumbents could add CRO templates once demand becomes visible.

structure.control_point: the credential-checked work record and equipment-card update created at completion of regulated service
structure.critical_dependency: accurate translation of Polish CRO and changing EU certification rules into low-friction technician workflows

thesis: Create a mobile-first evidence and compliance operating system for small Polish heat-pump, air-conditioning, and refrigeration service companies. A technician scans the asset, the system verifies the personnel and company certificate scope, records refrigerant and work performed, produces the customer's service proof, and prepares the operator's equipment-card update in the Polish CRO. Refrigerant wholesalers, equipment distributors, and certification-training providers are natural repeat distributors because they already serve thousands of small installers; the founder's family renewable-energy company offers a bounded design-partner environment. The moat is an installed-equipment service graph linking certified people, companies, assets, refrigerant movements, and audit-ready procedures, not a static checklist.
title: CRO ServiceProof for Heat-Pump and Refrigeration Firms
uncertainties: Whether CRO exposes an integration route or requires assisted/manual transfer
Actual willingness of wholesalers and training providers to distribute independent software
Paid demand among very small installers versus reliance on spreadsheets and the public portal
